newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Bank Negara seeks banks' lending compliance plans.
newsitem.headline: Bank Negara seeks banks' lending compliance plans.

text.p: Bank Negara Malaysia on Thursday met chief executives of Malaysian financial institutions to explain the new lending guidelines and seek their compliance plans, senior bankers said.
They said Bank Negara wanted banks exceeding the new lending limit to property sector to submit their compliance plans by April 15.
No information was available from the central bank.
Bank Negara last Friday announced that bank system's lending to the property shall not exceed 20 percent of each institution's total outstanding loans.
But the new rule, effective from April 1, exempted loans for houses costing below 150,000 ringgit, finance for infrastructure projects and schools and industrial buildings.

"Compliance will be on a quarterly basis. Consequently, from the quarter beginning April 1 to June 30, 1997, credit facilities to the broad property sector shall, on average, amount to not more than 20 percent of the loan base," a banker said reading from a statement issued by the central bank.
He said the average monthly loans outstanding at the end of January, February and March would form the loan base for compliance in the second quater of the year.

"Banking institutions which have exceeded the limit as at end-March 1997 are required to submit concrete plans to Bank Negara Malaysia on measures they would undertake to comply with the 20 percent limit .... not later than April 15, 1997," he said, reading from the statement.
The central bank had said the current limit of 15 percent on a bank's total loans given against pledge of shares and units of unit trust funds was being widened.
The 15 percent restriction would now also include lending for purchase of shares and units of unit trust funds. The limit stands unchanged at 30 percent for merchant banks.

"This restriction (15 percent) will now be redefined to cover credit facilities extended for the purchase of shares and units of unit trust funds," the central bank statement was quoted as saying by bankers.
Compliance to the lending rule for purchase of shares will also be quarterly and banks exceeding the limits shall have to submit plans for reducing their exposure, the bankers said.
They said for the purposes of the new guidelines, credit facilities would include all forms of lending, including issue of guarantees.
